newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan trade surplus jumps 163.7 percent in April.
newsitem.headline: Japan trade surplus jumps 163.7 percent in April.

text.p: Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus more than doubled in April from a year earlier to 831.48 billion yen, the Finance Ministry said on Monday.
The trade surplus with the United States, often a source of friction, surged 174.1 percent in April from a year earlier to 468.97 billion yen. The figures were not adjusted for seasonal factors.
The overall surplus rose 163.7 percent and was equivalent to $7.23 billion at Monday morning's dollar/yen exchange rate of about 115 yen to the dollar.

A Reuters poll of economists had produced an average forecast for the overall surplus of 821.8 billion yen ($7.14 billion), against a 315.3 billion yen ($2.74 billion) surplus a year ago. The forecasts for the surplus had ranged from 543 billion yen ($4.72 billion) to 940 billion yen ($8.17 billion).

Economists said the impact of the yen's weakness against the dollar from the the start of the year was filtering through. Exports were supported by strong overseas demand and the currency factor, which made exports more price competitive, they said. A rise in Japan's consumption tax to five percent from three percent from April 1 also contributed to the growth in the surplus, encouraging firms to emphasise exports amid sluggish demand at home, economists said.
The United States has expressed concern over Japan's rising trade surplus and has urged Japan to pursue an economic recovery led by domestic demand. ($1=115 yen)
